video_title: Windy believes that OKC might be ‘checkmated by the 7’4" guy’ Victor Wembanyama 😬 | Get Up

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Dean Wade's effective defense against Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: When Wade was the primary defender Monica, Jalen was 1 of 16.
quotes.quote: He might end up being right because the Cavs are not a strong defensive team, but they do have a guy that they used on him in the regular season that was very effective and that's 6'10" Dean Wade, who I expect to be back in the starting lineup tonight after he did not start Game 7. When Wade was the primary defender Monica, Jalen was 1 of 16. Now, I'm really cautious about going over reaction on a three-game regular season situation where they're back-to-backs and whatnot. But this is who the Cavs will rely on to be the primary defender and with Max Strus off the bench.

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' dramatic team improvement beyond Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: This has changed dramatically in two years. The trade of Julius Randle for Karl-Anthony Towns, how does that look right about now?
quotes.quote: So two years ago when the playoffs I did a rant that people in New York seem to really like when I talked about how Brunson, any criticism of Brunson was ridiculous because he was carrying this team basically by himself and if you looked at the roster man for man and what the output that they were getting, the production they were getting from other places, that it was ridiculous to point any finger of blame at him even if he played a bad game. This team is different. This has changed dramatically in two years. The trade of Julius Randle for Karl-Anthony Towns, how does that look right about now after the series that Randle just had? Towns, sometimes you have to listen to people when they talk to you. It's a good lesson for me even after 30 years doing this because Towns kept saying, 'I don't need more shots, I just want the ball.' And I'm thinking, that's another way of saying I want more shots. He was actually telling you the truth. He wanted to be more involved in the offense. He has been. Anunoby has emerged as a legitimate star assuming he is healthy. So while Brunson is still the best player on the team, they have so many other places they can go. To me, that's the difference in these Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' dynamic defense and Donovan Mitchell's scoring ability
quotes.excerpt: the Cavs have a player in Donovan Mitchell who can take a game.
quotes.quote: First off, the Cavs have a player in Donovan Mitchell who can take a game. He had a 39-point half in the last round. I wouldn't say he's playing his best basketball, but they have a guy who can come in and has come into Madison Square Garden in the past and taken a game from them. That's a big key. The second thing is, the Cavs do have a very malleable defense. They can switch and stuff like that. They do have good big men defenders. Jarrett Allen has come off a couple of very important games in this playoff career. The Cavs are more dynamic than the Sixers were. This is a different challenge. The Cavs are maddeningly inconsistent in everything that they do and that has driven their fans crazy. They are not a team that is a four-seed talent-wise. They are a team defensively and consistency-wise who are a four-seed.

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's game felt historically significant
quotes.excerpt: last night had a little bit of that kind of feel with Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: that felt like we may someday look back on it and say that's when everything changed. Michael Jordan makes that shot against Cleveland in Game 5 in 1989. We just had the anniversary of it recently, Windy, we were talking about it. You could almost break everything up into everything that came before that and everything that came since. I know that this might sound like hyperbole, but last night had a little bit of that kind of feel with Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder potentially 'checkmated' by Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: what if they're checkmated though? What if they're checkmated by the 7'5" guy?
quotes.quote: I have so much respect for the Oklahoma City Thunder organization. If you know about how they do things behind the scenes and how they are so researched and how I've seen them go through their own heartbreak and rebuild the team. And they have put together this team meticulously and beautifully. And as I'm watching this, I'm like, what if they're checkmated though? What if they're checkmated by the 7'5" guy? Because honestly, I'm just, I think of it like this, I'll keep saying it. You don't just have to beat him. You got to beat him four in seven. Four in seven. That mountain is looking like it's really hard to climb.

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama exceeding impossible expectations with Spurs
quotes.excerpt: Both of those somehow managed to exceed impossible expectations. This kid seems to be doing that right now.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Greenberg
text_blocks.text: You know what makes me think of is that every now and again a great one comes along of whom everything is expected and they outdo it. Hembo and I did a book in which we pointed out Wayne Gretzky when he was, I want to say he was 12 years old, there were headlines in the papers already locally comparing him to to the greatest literally the greatest players, Gordie Howe, the greatest players of all time. LeBron James when he came into the league had as much fanfare as any player coming in directly out of high school. Both of those somehow managed to exceed impossible expectations. This kid seems to be doing that right now.

text_blocks.speaker: Marcus Spears
text_blocks.text: He seems to be doing that. And when you think of the great players that came before him, that's what makes it crazy. You have the Admiral. Of course, you had Tim Duncan. And he's doing this. This is wild.

text_blocks.speaker: Monica McNutt
text_blocks.text: And what does he have in common with those guys? The organization that he lands in. And so I think skill, focus, all of those things, but you got to give the Spurs a tip of the cap.
